t: I keep telling it because I am still trying to understand it.
Every time I say it aloud, part of it sounds less certain.
I know what I saw. I do not know what I should call it.
Maybe I have added something without meaning to. I have told it often.
The facts stay the same. My opinion changes every time.
I was certain yesterday. Today I can see the gaps.
I have heard myself tell this enough to know where I hesitate.
Some days it sounds like the god. Some days it sounds like fear.
I am not changing the story. I am changing around it.
The more people ask what it meant, the less certain I become.
I wish seeing a thing made its meaning obvious.
I still believe something happened. That is the firmest part.
I have told it straight each time. Straight does not mean complete.
Ask what happened and I can answer. Ask why and I cannot.
I keep waiting for somebody else to explain what I witnessed.
The story has settled. I have not.
I believe my eyes, but my eyes did not explain themselves.
Perhaps I will know what I think after I stop repeating it.
I am closer to belief than I was, but not close enough to claim it.
That is everything I know and only half of what I suspect.
I have told it often because people should know what the god did.
The story does not weaken with telling. It becomes clearer.
I was there, and every telling confirms what I already believed.
People may tire of hearing it. The truth does not tire.
I repeat it because gratitude should not become quiet.
The god acted openly. I will speak about it openly.
Every person I tell becomes another person who remembers.
I have not changed one word that matters.
The god gave us a story worth keeping. I intend to keep it.
I know how it sounds. I also know what I witnessed.
The story becomes less believable every time I hear myself repeat it.
I have told the facts. Other people keep adding the god.
Repetition does not make an explanation true.
I saw something strange. I did not see a divine hand.
People remember the frightening part and improve the rest.
I keep correcting the story, and people keep preferring the larger version.
What happened was odd enough without turning it into doctrine.
I should stop telling it before people mistake me for a believer.
The event was real. The god is somebody else's addition.
I have repeated it exactly. Exact stories can still be misunderstood.
I can almost believe that. Almost is doing a lot of work.
You have given me more to think about than I wanted.
That sounds possible, which is not the same as true.
I am listening. I am not promising where I will land.
Part of that fits. Part of it still catches.
I would have laughed last year. I am not laughing now.
You may be right. I dislike how easily I can say that.
I need one more account before I trust my first reaction.
My doubt is smaller than it was five minutes ago.
I cannot dismiss it, and I cannot accept it yet.
The god's hand is plain in that. I believe you.
Thank you for telling me. People should hear what the god has done.
That fits what I already know of the god.
I had no doubt before, and I have less now.
We should remember this properly and not let it become idle talk.
I believe you saw something. That is where my agreement ends.
There will be an ordinary cause somewhere in that story.
People reach for the god when the facts are incomplete.
I need evidence, not another confident voice.
Strange does not automatically mean divine.
